correctness.rationale: For all a,b>=1 and k>=2, single-letter and transition-factor necessity yields exactly the listed families. The independent occurrence-interval lemma shows any central position attracts every length-at-least-period factor of a primitive-period power. Each candidate family has a central position. Shorter factors have at most two transitions; direct embedding at selected oriented transitions, or at singleton runs with both flanking full runs, attracts all of them. This proves the all-pair theorem and the exact distinct counts. The actual bundled verify.py passed 360 parameter cases and matched all pairs against full factor dictionaries; finite evidence is supplementary, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: All optimal string-attractor position sets, not just the minimum size, are mathematically natural and studied in the literature as measures of repetition and compression structure. The theorem gives a complete infinite-parameter classification with a sharp singleton-run transition; in the non-singleton regime the number 2k(k-1) is independent of run lengths, while singleton runs produce (k-1)(k max(a,b)+1). It also proves a special equivalence of 2-attractor and full attractor tests for this family; neither part is a mere fixed table or tautological rewriting.
